Eucalyptus cunninghamii was first formally described in 1991 by Ian Brooker and Stephen Hopper from a specimen collected by Brooker in 1986. The description was published in the journal Nuytsia. The specific epithet (cunninghamii) honours the botanist and explorer, William Cunningham.

Distribution and habitat
Cunningham's gum grows in open forest and woodland in the Avon Wheatbelt, Coolgardie, Esperance Plains, Jarrah Forest and Mallee biogeographic regions. It is found between Kalgoorlie and Esperance.

Conservation status
This eucalypt is classified as "not threatened" by the Western Australian Government Department of Parks and Wildlife.

**Background:** The aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a new, highly purified, humanized anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody (mAb) in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL).

**Methods:** In this open-label, multicenter, phase II study, patients with r/r B-cell NHL were treated with the anti-CD20 mAb obinutuzumab (GA101) at a dose of 1000 mg every 2 weeks. The primary endpoint was the overall response rate (ORR) at week 24. Secondary endpoints included the ORR at week 48, the duration of response (DOR), the progression-free survival (PFS), and the safety profile.

**Results:** A total of 40 patients were enrolled in the study. The median age was 63 years (range, 27--83 years), and the median number of prior therapies was 2 (range, 1--6). The most common types of NHL were diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (n=20, 50%) and follicular lymphoma (n=10, 25%). The ORR at week 24 was 80% (95% confidence interval \[CI\], 68--92), with a complete response (CR) rate of 50% (95% CI, 34--66). The median DOR was not reached, and the median PFS was not reached. The most common adverse events (AEs) were neutropenia (n=32, 80%), thrombocytopenia (n=28, 70%), and anemia (n=25, 62.5%). The most common grade 3/4 AEs were neutropenia (n=18, 45%) and thrombocytopenia (n=14, 35%). The most common serious AEs were neutropenia (n=12, 30%) and thrombocytopenia (n=8, 20%). The most common grade 3/4 infections were pneumonia (n=3, 7.5%) and sepsis (n=2, 5%). The most common grade 3/4 AEs related to infusion-related reactions were chills (n=3, 7.5%) and fever (n=2, 5%).

**Conclusions:** The ORR at week 24 was 80%, and the DOR was not reached. The safety profile was consistent with the known safety profile of obinutuzumab.

General information

The municipality of Hjørundfjorden was established on 1 January 1838 (see formannskapsdistrikt).  The initial population of the municipality was 1,972.  On 1 January 1875, the northern part of the municipality was separated to form the new municipality of Tana.  On 1 January 1884, the western part of the municipality was separated to form the new municipality of Vardø.  On 1 January 1917, the eastern part of the municipality was separated to form the new municipality of Alta.  On 1 January 1923, the eastern part of the municipality was separated to form the new municipality of Hammerfest.  On 1 January 1924, the northern part of the municipality was separated to form the new municipality of Sør-Varanger.  On 1 January 1965, the municipality of Hjørundfjorden was merged with the municipalities of Alta, Tana, and Vardø to form a new, larger municipality of Alta.  On 1 January 2002, the municipality of Hjørundfjorden was merged with the municipalities of Tana and Vardø to form a new, larger municipality of Tana.

On the morning of March 5, 1992, Officer Michael D. Smith of the Kansas City, Missouri, Police Department was on routine patrol in a marked police car.  He was driving south on a four-lane street in Kansas City, Missouri, when he observed a vehicle driven by the defendant, a black male, traveling north in the same direction.  The defendant was driving at a speed of approximately thirty-five to forty-five miles per hour in a thirty-five mile per hour speed zone.  Officer Smith testified that he observed the defendant's vehicle weave within its lane of travel, cross the center line, and then return to the center line.  Officer Smith also testified that the defendant's vehicle was weaving in a manner that was "consistent with somebody who was under the influence of alcohol or drugs."   Officer Smith then stopped the defendant's vehicle.


3
Officer Smith approached the defendant's vehicle and asked the defendant for his driver's license and vehicle registration.  The defendant told Officer Smith that he was driving a rental car.  Officer Smith then asked the defendant to step out of the vehicle.  Officer Smith testified that he noticed that the defendant was "very nervous" and "very fidgety."   Officer Smith also testified that the defendant was "sweating profusely" and that his eyes were "very bloodshot."   Officer Smith then asked the defendant if he had been drinking.  The defendant responded that he had consumed two beers.  Officer Smith then asked the defendant to perform several field sobriety tests.  The defendant failed to perform the tests satisfactorily.  Officer Smith then placed the defendant under arrest for driving under the influence of alcohol.  Officer Smith then searched the defendant's vehicle and found a plastic bag containing a white powdery substance in the glove compartment.  The substance was later determined to be cocaine.


4
The defendant contends that the district court erred in denying his motion to suppress the cocaine found in his vehicle.  He argues that the stop of his vehicle was not supported by reasonable suspicion.  We disagree.


5
We review the district court's findings of fact for clear error and its conclusions of law de novo.
